title: Image thumbnails decode every file at full size and are never freed
problem: `file_icon` draws thumbnails for common image formats up to 40 MB with `img(entry.path.clone())` (src/finder/views.rs:110-137), used by the icon grid (views.rs:504), the gallery strip (views.rs:1299) and Get Info (src/finder/info.rs:297). This branch runs before, and bypasses, the on-disk thumbnail cache in src/thumbnails.rs (views.rs:138-151), even though the manual says thumbnails come from the system thumbnailer. GPUI's loader reads the whole file and decodes every pixel with no downscale (gpui-pre-0.3.10/src/elements/img.rs:634, 735) and keeps the result: 'Pending loads and completed results are cached until remove_asset' (gpui-pre-0.3.10/src/app.rs:3160). fffinder never calls `remove_asset` and uses no image cache (the only release in src is `cx.drop_image` for PDF pages, src/finder/pdf.rs:265-267). So scrolling an icon view or gallery strip over a photo folder holds each photo as full-size BGRA for the life of the app (a 12 MP JPEG is about 48 MB, so 200 photos is roughly 9.6 GB) and uploads each at full size to the GPU atlas to draw a 64 to 128 point tile. The large preview has the same leak (`img(entry.path.clone())`, src/finder/preview.rs:905). Because the asset is keyed by path alone, an image rewritten in place keeps showing its old pixels even after Refresh, which only clears `previews` (src/finder/mod.rs:1200).
proposal: 1) thumbnails.rs: add a cross-platform in-process thumbnailer `make_image(file, px, out) -> Option<()>` using the existing `image` dependency: `image::ImageReader::open(file)?.with_guessed_format()?.decode()?.thumbnail(px, px)` saved as PNG. In `cached()` (thumbnails.rs:173-188) try it first for png/jpg/jpeg/gif/webp/bmp/ico/tif/tiff and fall back to the platform `make`. It runs on the three thumbnail threads and lands in the existing (path, mtime, px) PNG cache with its 256 MB prune. Add explicit `png`, `jpeg`, `gif`, `webp`, `bmp`, `tiff`, `ico` features to `image` in Cargo.toml (gpui already enables them, so nothing new is compiled). 2) views.rs `file_icon`: drop the `img(entry.path)` branch for raster images so they go through `thumbnails::image(entry, px)` like PDFs and videos (keep SVG as it is; it is small). 3) Large preview: track the image paths recently shown large on `Finder` (a `VecDeque` of 3) in `ensure_preview`; on overflow, or when an entry's `modified` differs from the one recorded, release the old one with `cx.fetch_asset::<ImgResourceLoader>` + `cx.drop_image` (deferred, as pdf.rs:265-267) and `ImageSource::remove_asset` (gpui-pre img.rs:577). 4) Add `.with_loading(spinner)` to the large `img` (preview.rs:905-917 has only `with_fallback`), so a slow decode shows a spinner instead of an empty area.
original_test_plan: Unit test in thumbnails.rs: write a 1200x600 PNG with `image::RgbaImage`, call `make_image(&file, 128, &out)`, assert `image::image_dimensions(&out) == (128, 64)`, and that an undecodable file returns None. Headless UI tests (tests/controls.rs): put `photo.png` in the fixture, show the icon view, and assert `ui.window(|_, cx| gpui_kit::ImageSource::from(path.clone()).is_asset_cached(cx))` is false (GPUI's test-support helper, img.rs:588-596), i.e. the grid no longer loads the original. In the gallery, select five PNGs in turn and assert at most three are `is_asset_cached`. Rewrite one with a new mtime, reload, and assert its asset was dropped.
original_risks: The first visit to a photo folder decodes on three threads instead of GPUI's whole pool, so tiles fill in a little slower; afterwards they come from disk. On macOS and Windows the system thumbnailer could be used instead of the in-process one; trying in-process first keeps all platforms identical and testable on Linux. Two panes showing the same image share one asset, so evicting in one makes the other reload it once. UI tests keep icons because `thumbnails::image` is disabled under the test Recorder (thumbnails.rs:79-85); no existing test uses image files.

verifier.claim_check:
The problem is real; I could not refute it. Two of the four proposed steps need correcting.

**Confirmed**
- `src/finder/views.rs:129-137`: `file_icon` returns `img(entry.path.clone())` for png/jpg/jpeg/gif/webp/bmp/ico/tif/tiff/svg up to 40 MB (`thumbnailable`, 110-124), before the `thumbnails::image` branch at 138-151. It is used with `thumbnails = true` by the icon grid (views.rs:504), the gallery strip (views.rs:1299) and Get Info (`src/finder/info.rs:297`).
- GPUI reads the whole file and decodes at full size: `gpui-pre-0.3.10/src/elements/img.rs:634` (`fs::read`), 735 (`decode_static_image`), and `platform.rs:3335-3350` (`into_rgba8`, no downscale). A GIF decodes every frame (img.rs:671-698), although an `img` without an id never animates.
- The result is kept in `App.loading_assets` until `remove_asset` (`app.rs:3145-3176`). `paint_image` uploads the full-size frame to the sprite atlas (`window.rs:5095-5105`).
- fffinder has no `remove_asset`, no `image_cache`, and only one `drop_image`, for PDF pages (`src/finder/pdf.rs:265-267`). The grid is virtualized (views.rs:408), so the cost grows with every tile scrolled past.
- The large preview does the same with no size cap: `src/finder/preview.rs:905`, reached from the gallery, the column card, the preview pane and Quick Look.
- Stale pixels are real too: the asset key is `Resource::Path` alone, and `refresh` (`src/finder/mod.rs:1199-1207`) only clears `previews`.
- Not covered elsewhere: `CHANGELOG.md` has nothing on this, and no file in `tests/*.rs` uses an image file or pins this behaviour.

**Inaccurate in the proposal**
- The direct GPUI path is documented, not accidental: `docs/manual.md:238` lists these formats "up to 40 MB", and the `src/thumbnails.rs:1-2` header says the system draws "images GPUI can't decode". Only the unbounded retention is unintended.
- Step 1's `ImageReader::decode()` ignores EXIF orientation, which GPUI applies today (`platform.rs:3338-3342`). Phone photos would turn sideways.
- Step 3 hooks `ensure_preview`, which returns early when the path is already in `previews` (`preview.rs:311`). A revisited image would never be re-tracked and would leak again. `cx.fetch_asset` also starts a load when the path is not cached (`app.rs:3165-3170`).
- Step 4 does nothing as written. `Img` shows its loading element only when it has an element id (`img.rs:289-296, 400-421`), and the `img` at `preview.rs:905` has none. The existing `.with_loading(icon)` at `views.rs:149` and `preview.rs:1126` is inert for the same reason, so tiles are blank while loading, contrary to `manual.md:416`.
verifier.implementation_notes:
**1. `src/thumbnails.rs`: in-process thumbnailer**
- Add a cross-platform `fn make_image(file: &Path, px: u32, out: &Path) -> Option<()>`.
- Skip files over 40 MB (`fs::metadata`), so `manual.md:238` stays true and larger files still go to the platform `make`.
- Decode the way GPUI does, to keep EXIF rotation:
  - `ImageReader::open(file).ok()?.with_guessed_format().ok()?.into_decoder().ok()?`
  - read `decoder.orientation()`, then `DynamicImage::from_decoder(decoder)`, then `apply_orientation`.
- Keep the default `Limits` (512 MiB), or set a lower one.
- Put the resize in a pure helper, `fn shrink(image: DynamicImage, px: u32) -> DynamicImage`:
  - return the image unchanged when it already fits in px by px, because `DynamicImage::thumbnail` upscales;
  - otherwise `thumbnail(px, px)`.
- Convert to RGBA8 before saving, so 16-bit and float TIFFs encode. Save with `save_with_format(out, ImageFormat::Png)`.
- In `cached()` (173-188), try `make_image` first for png/jpg/jpeg/gif/webp/bmp/ico/tif/tiff, matched on the lowercased extension, then fall back to the platform `make(&key.0, key.2, &partial)`.
- Using it first on every platform keeps today's plain look. QuickLook's icon mode would add a border (`src/macos.rs:234`).
- Update the module doc comment.

**2. `Cargo.toml`**
- `image = { version = "0.25", default-features = false, features = ["png","jpeg","gif","webp","bmp","tiff","ico"] }`.
- gpui-pre already enables all of these (its Cargo.toml:365-383), and `Cargo.lock` has a single `image 0.25.10`, so nothing new is compiled.

**3. `src/finder/views.rs`**
- Narrow `thumbnailable` to SVG only; rename it (for example `draws_itself`).
- Raster images then fall through to the existing `thumbnails::wanted` branch, since `FileKind::Image` is already wanted (`thumbnails.rs:37`). They get the (path, mtime, px) key, which also fixes stale tiles.
- Recommended: give that `img` an id, `.id(("thumb", path_id(&entry.path)))`, so the existing `.with_loading(icon)` takes effect and tiles show the kind icon while queued. Raster tiles now wait on three threads.

**4. Large preview: replace the proposed deque + `fetch_asset`/`remove_asset`**
- Use GPUI's public `ImageCacheItem` (`image_cache.rs:167-193`) in a small per-`Finder` LRU entity. A new `src/finder/preview_images.rs` or a section of `preview.rs` would hold it.
- Shape: `struct PreviewImages(VecDeque<((PathBuf, Option<SystemTime>), ImageCacheItem)>)`, with `KEEP = 3`.
- `load(key, window, cx)`:
  - move a hit to the back;
  - on a miss, push `ImageCacheItem::new(&Resource::Path(..), cx)`;
  - evict the front past `KEEP`, and any entry with the same path but another mtime, calling `cx.drop_image(image, Some(window))` when `item.get()` is `Some(Ok(image))`.
- Return `item.use_image(window)`.
- Create the entity in `Finder::new` (`mod.rs:467`, fields near 327). Add `cx.observe_release` to drop its images, copying `RetainAllImageCache::new` (`image_cache.rs:235-246`).
- At `preview.rs:905`, replace `img(entry.path.clone())` with an `ImageSource::Custom` closure that captures the entity and `(path, modified)` and calls `cache.update(cx, |c, cx| c.load(&key, window, cx))`. This is the same pattern as `thumbnails::image`.
- Why this shape:
  - every large load is bounded wherever `preview_body` is called (gallery, column card, preview pane, Quick Look);
  - nothing depends on `ensure_preview` call sites;
  - a rewritten file reloads because the key includes mtime;
  - closing a tab frees its images;
  - one pane cannot evict another pane's image.
- A capacity of 3 per pane cannot thrash, because a pane shows at most one large image plus Quick Look.

**5. Drop step 4 from this change**
- A spinner needs `.id(..)` on the large `img`.
- An id also switches on GIF/WebP animation and continuous `request_animation_frame` (`img.rs:321-388`). That is a behaviour change, with a cost in `--term` mode, and should be decided separately.

**6. Docs**
- `docs/manual.md`: Thumbnails section (406-416) and the data-folder line (1177), to say fffinder draws image thumbnails itself on every system and caches them.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: an entry under Unreleased.

**Pitfalls**
- `thumbnails::image` returns an error under the test `Recorder` (`thumbnails.rs:79-85`), so UI tests cannot see a drawn thumbnail, only that the original is not loaded.
- `Window::drop_image` is called mid-layout; GPUI's own `RetainAllImageCache::remove` does the same.
- SVG tiles and the decoded thumbnail PNGs (64 KB to 1 MB each) are still never freed. That is the same retention PDFs and videos already have.
verifier.test_plan:
**Unit tests in `src/thumbnails.rs`** (existing `mod tests`, plain `#[test]`; the dev-dependency `image` already has `png`)
- Write a 1200x600 `image::RgbaImage` PNG to a temp dir, call `make_image(&file, 128, &out)`, and assert `image::image_dimensions(&out).unwrap() == (128, 64)`.
- A 20x10 PNG stays 20x10 (no upscaling).
- A file of garbage bytes returns `None`.
- The pure `shrink` helper on a 1200x600 image after `apply_orientation(Orientation::Rotate90)` gives 64x128. This guards rotation without needing an EXIF fixture.

**Headless UI tests in `tests/controls.rs`**
- Helpers from `tests/common/mod.rs`: `Fixture::new`, `Ui::open`, `ui.click("view-gallery")`, `ui.select(name)`, `ui.exists(item_id("tile", &p))`, `ui.window(..)`, `ui.read(..)`. Write the PNGs into `fx.dir` with `image::RgbaImage::new(8, 8).save(..)` before `Ui::open`.
- Test 1, icon view (the default view in tests):
  - assert `ui.exists(item_id("tile", &photo))`;
  - assert `!ui.window(|_, cx| gpui_kit::ImageSource::from(photo.clone()).is_asset_cached(cx))`.
  - `is_asset_cached` is GPUI's test-support helper (`img.rs:589-596`). The assertion is true before the change, because `use_asset` inserts the entry during layout, and false after.
- Test 2, gallery:
  - click `view-gallery`, then `ui.select` five PNGs in turn;
  - assert a new `Finder::preview_image_count_for_test()` (beside `has_preview_for_test`, `mod.rs:706`) is at most 3;
  - assert none of the five paths `is_asset_cached` in the global cache.
- Test 3, rewritten file:
  - rewrite one PNG and set a new mtime with `File::set_modified`;
  - dispatch `Refresh` and settle;
  - assert the cache holds that path once, with the new mtime, through a small test accessor.

GPUI's loader runs on the deterministic test executor, so `ui.settle()` completes the loads. I did not run cargo, per the task.
verifier.risks:
- **Rotation regression** if the thumbnailer uses `ImageReader::decode()` as proposed. It must read the decoder's orientation and apply it, as GPUI does.
- **Slower first fill.** The first visit to a photo folder decodes on three FIFO thumbnail threads instead of GPUI's whole pool, and a hung Linux thumbnailer can hold one of them for 10 s. A fast scroll queues every tile passed, with no cancellation. Revisits read small PNGs from disk. Raising the thread count or serving newest jobs first is an optional follow-up.
- **Blank tiles while queued** unless the thumbnail `img` gets an id; `with_loading` is inert without one.
- **Thumbnails of the user's photos are now written to `thumbnails/` in the data folder.** This already happens for PDFs, videos and HEIC, within the 256 MB prune, which only runs at startup.
- **Resize quality.** `DynamicImage::thumbnail` is a fast box scaler on non-premultiplied alpha, so transparent edges may fringe slightly. It should still look better than the GPU minifying a 4000 px texture.
- **Transient memory.** Each decode can take up to 512 MiB under the default `Limits`, across three threads.
- **Residual retention.** Decoded thumbnail PNGs and SVGs stay in GPUI's asset cache, roughly 200 to 750 times smaller per file than today.
- **Split panes** showing the same image decode it once per pane.
- **UI tests** cannot observe a drawn thumbnail, because thumbnails are disabled under the `Recorder`.

orchestrator_notes: No new dependency unless there is truly no other way; the `image` crate is already a dependency (check its enabled features in Cargo.toml before relying on a decoder). Image orientation must not regress.
